A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C2EC dataset and training-free correction framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support comparison, including identification of relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original correction experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative analyses on CSCD-NS, Lemon, and C2EC.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds SIGHAN evaluations and precision–recall sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix F.3 introduces an adjustable distance-penalty coefficient γ in Equation 14, adding control over decoding. The main configuration uses γ = 1 and retains the original dual-LLM, weighted-Levenshtein procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on SIGHAN13, SIGHAN14, and SIGHAN15, previously discussed only as prior work. This extends the real-error evaluations on CSCD-NS, Lemon, and C2EC to the classical CSC benchmark collection, whose different domain and error-pattern characteristics are discussed in Section 8.1.

E2.justification: The new SIGHAN comparison adds SpellGCN, ReaLiSe, DISC-enhanced variants, SCOPE+DR-CSC, and GPT3.5/GPT4, using previously reported comparison scores (v2 Table 10). This substantially expands the comparator panel beyond the retained training-free and supervised comparisons.

E3.justification: The added SIGHAN evaluation reports sentence-level detection and correction precision, recall, and F1, with SIGHAN13 post-processing described in Table 10. v2 also introduces temperature and γ sweeps. Original dataset splits and primary correction metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3 and Figure 12 add sensitivity analyses testing how temperature and distance weighting affect precision, recall, and F1. Earlier component, model-family, model-size, beam-size, error-type, and qualitative analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages for randomized ICL and single-run greedy results for API models. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial SIGHAN detection/correction results, precision–recall curves, and explicit Qwen2.5 development scores in Table 5. Original main-table results remain unchanged. Exact new SIGHAN scores are questionable: Table 10 lists 7B detection P = 51.1, R = 47.2, and F1 = 55.6 on SIGHAN14, indicating an apparent column-order error.

T1.justification: Equation 14 adds a parameterized scoring definition with γ weighting the distance term. The distance definitions, reinforcement-learning derivation, and optimal-policy proof in Appendices B–C remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the C2EC task and real-error dataset, a training-free extension of TfPf, and competitive performance from a 14B model against models nearly 50 times larger.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that its method trails classical models trained on SIGHAN (Appendix E.3). Appendix F.3 adds application guidance: distance weighting is more effective for increasing precision, while temperature is more effective for increasing recall.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents per-ablation temperature tuning, DeepSeek model release dates, and the default γ value. These improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Hardware, implementation approximations, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qiao et al. (2024), the DISC paper, as the source for the SIGHAN comparisons. The remaining bibliography and substantive research positioning in Section 8 are retained.

P1.justification: The LLM-family study moves from Appendix F.1 to Section 7.5, and the matched-model SFT comparison moves from F.4 to E.2. Cross-references, acknowledgments, and several explanations are revised, including correction of the discarded-annotation example; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds SIGHAN Table 10 and precision–recall Figure 12, adds English examples and revised colors to Figure 1, resizes retained plots, and expands the relocated LLM-family table. Most existing figures and tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new precision–recall study and clearer experimental disclosures provide useful application and reproducibility guidance. The SIGHAN comparison makes performance limitations more explicit, although its apparent P/R/F1 column errors weaken the added numerical evidence. With the original evidence retained, these additions provide a modest net improvement.
